o1.biggest_strength: A ranked, ticket-driven plan with the three articles written in our voice, a forecasted range with visible working, and per-screen link changes — exactly the decision I asked for.
o1.biggest_mistake: The forecast is a blanket 25–50% saved across all three articles with one assumption, which is thin; it also stops short of saying which numbers depend on the engineer's day landing in time, and skips the currency/merge items from the forecast entirely (it says so, but it undersells the currency gap as a lever).
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Per-article, justified save rates (like 40% for delete because it already helps 64% of readers) and a currency article drafted or at least scoped, with the in-app link timing built into the low/high range.

o2.biggest_strength: Per-article save rates with a stated reason for each, plus the currency article counted in the forecast, and a bonus currency-relevant step in the link changes; the refund and cancel distinction is clear.
o2.biggest_mistake: Item 5 merges "Recording a payment" — which is already 71% helpful — into a "Settle up" article; that's work for little gain and risks wrecking a good article, and it contradicts its own "already helpful" note. The forecast is a single point (3,700) with only a half-share floor, not a range.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Don't touch the 71%-helpful article; give a proper low/high range with working like the other output, and show the currency forecast's assumptions more plainly.

reason: Both are publishable and in our voice; output 2's forecast shows its thinking article by article and counts the currency gap, which I trust more, but output 1's range and its hands-off the one good article are real advantages — this is close. Output 2 edges it on reasoning and honesty, despite the odd merge of a working article.
